scoring: Each check is pass/fail. A dimension scores 1 only if every one of its checks passes. Phase 8 score = number of passing dimensions (0-5); 5 only if all checks pass. A manual check passes only with its evidence file committed. Criteria are never loosened after results are seen; a failure is fixed at its cause or reported as a failure (as in Phase 7/7b).

check_kinds.code: checked by python -m dashboards.verify_phase8 (and its tests); runs in CI on Linux
check_kinds.code_local: needs the local database or the deployed app; checked by verify_phase8 --local and recorded with its output in dashboards/local_checks.json, committed
check_kinds.manual: checked against docs/PHASE8_CHECKLIST.md with the named screenshot or file committed under docs/figures/phase8/

tolerances.floats_recomputed_independently: absolute 1e-9 (ratios 1e-12); different summation order is the only allowed difference
tolerances.displayed_values: the rounded string on the page equals the independently recomputed value rounded the same way
tolerances.powerbi_exports: equal to the independent value at the precision shown in the report

checks.check: Every number listed in phase8_spec.json pages[].numbers, as rendered by the Streamlit app (AppTest), equals the independent recomputation from the raw results files within the stated tolerance
Every snapshot file matches the manifest: row count, sha256, key unique and sorted, run IDs
Snapshot values equal the independent files cell for cell (fleet, models, plan, work orders, OEE machines, OEE policies, monitoring)
Snapshots of public.* tables equal PostgreSQL cell for cell (CI verify job, after maintenance.store)
Snapshots of ops and ops7b_* tables equal PostgreSQL cell for cell (local database; CI has no Phase 7 replay of all shifts)
Every number in docs/DASHBOARDS.md and every Phase 8 number in README.md equals the independent value
Power BI exported values (docs/figures/phase8/powerbi_exports/*.csv) equal the independent values at displayed precision
python -m dashboards.export_snapshots run twice gives byte-identical files (same sha256) equal to the committed ones
CI job installs ONLY app/requirements.txt (exact pins) into a clean Python and runs the AppTest suite from a fresh checkout
CI runs dashboards.verify_phase8 on Linux and it passes; the committed manifest's source sha256 values equal the committed source files (snapshot not stale)
The deployed Streamlit Community Cloud app shows a data checksum equal to the repo manifest's data_checksum (screenshot docs/figures/phase8/deployed_about.png)
AppTest loads every page with every filter combination listed in the spec with no exception
A missing snapshot file, a corrupt one (bad sha256 or unparsable) and a filter that leaves no rows each show a clear st.error/st.info message and no exception
The verifier catches at least 5 planted bugs, each in a separate test: wrong OEE, off-by-one shift, dropped engine, stale snapshot (source changed), swapped interval bounds; plus wrong flagged count
Every page that shows OEE or simulated plant values contains the word 'Simulated' in its rendered text
The fleet page shows the interval with its nominal (90%) and observed coverage, and marks FD001's coverage as post hoc
The monitoring page shows the FD004 C1 failure ('FAIL') and the Phase 7 false-alarm target miss ('not met'), with their rates
Every st.metric has non-empty help text (its definition), and every required_text in the spec appears on its page
The published model (LSTM) and all baselines appear in one table on the same test engines per dataset
Each page's title is the question stated in the spec
Every chart uses only Okabe-Ito colours, and every colour encoding is paired with a second channel (shape, stroke dash, text label or axis position)
Every chart axis has a title, and every quantitative axis title names its unit in parentheses
Each page script runs in under 5 s in AppTest on the CI runner (script time; browser rendering is checked manually in D5.5)
Each page at 375 px phone width has no horizontal page scroll and readable charts (screenshots docs/figures/phase8/phone_<page>.png), and loads visibly in under 5 s locally

The Power BI report follows the same rules: question titles, Okabe-Ito colours with a second channel, axis titles with units, 'Simulated' on OEE pages (PDF docs/figures/phase8/powerbi_report.pdf and checklist)
